scenario: An observatory database stores exposure times only when they exceed 300 seconds. Astronomers want the mean exposure time across all captures.

data.description: Only exposures above 300 seconds are observed. Exposure time is Normal with known sigma 60 seconds.

question: Estimate (a) the true mean exposure time mu across all captures and (b) the fraction of captures stored in the database.
naive_answer: Average exposure is about 332 seconds because that is the database mean.
naive_trap: Short exposures are not kept in the database.
reasoning_trace: With alpha≈1.0, mu=300-60=240 and stored fraction sf(1)=0.1587.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(300-mu)/60; return mu+60*norm.pdf(a)/norm.sf(a)-331.51
mu=brentq(eq,-200,299.99)
frac=norm.sf((300-mu)/60)
assert abs(mu-240)<4 and abs(frac-0.1587)<0.005
